blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: A Secret stores small pieces of private data, such as a password. It comes from the core v1 API.
blocks.why: Secrets keep private data out of images and Pod files, and access can be limited separately.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.why: Pods find the Secret by this name.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: The name Pods use to find this Secret
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: db-login

blocks.title: The private values
blocks.what: stringData lets you write values as plain text. Kubernetes stores them base64-encoded under data.
blocks.why: Base64 is encoding, not encryption, so never commit real passwords to Git. These are dummy values.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Secret is created empty, so the app gets no login.
blocks.comment: The login details. Dummy values for practice only.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: db-login
type: Opaque
stringData:
  username: app-user
  password: change-me

blocks.title: A Pod to use it
blocks.what: Three dashes start a second object: a Pod called secret-demo.
blocks.why: The Pod shows how an app reads one value from the Secret.
blocks.ifRemoved: The file only stores the Secret. Nothing uses it yet.
blocks.comment: A Pod that uses the Secret
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: db-login
type: Opaque
stringData:
  username: app-user
  password: change-me
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secret-demo

blocks.title: What should run?
blocks.what: A small busybox container prints the username, then waits.
blocks.why: The username stays empty until the next block passes it in.
blocks.ifRemoved: Without containers, Kubernetes rejects the Pod.
blocks.comment: A container that prints the username
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: db-login
type: Opaque
stringData:
  username: app-user
  password: change-me
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secret-demo
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox:1.37.0
      command: ["sh", "-c", "echo Connecting as $DB_USER && sleep 3600"]

blocks.title: Pass in one value
blocks.what: env creates the variable DB_USER from the username key of the db-login Secret.
blocks.why: secretKeyRef picks one key, so the app gets only what it needs.
blocks.ifRemoved: DB_USER is empty, so the app cannot log in.
blocks.comment: Set DB_USER from one key of the Secret
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: db-login
type: Opaque
stringData:
  username: app-user
  password: change-me
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secret-demo
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox:1.37.0
      command: ["sh", "-c", "echo Connecting as $DB_USER && sleep 3600"]
      env:
        - name: DB_USER
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: db-login
              key: username

notes.---: Three dashes separate objects. One file can hold several objects.
notes.apiVersion: The API version for this object. Secrets and Pods are both in the core v1 API.
notes.Secret:kind: The type of object to create. A Secret stores small pieces of private data.
notes.Pod:kind: The type of object to create. A Pod runs one or more containers together.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.Secret:metadata.name: The Secret's name. Pods refer to it by this name.
notes.Pod:metadata.name: The Pod's name. It must be unique among Pods in the same namespace.
notes.type: Opaque means any data you choose. It is the default type.
notes.stringData: Values written as plain text. Kubernetes encodes them when it saves the Secret.
notes.stringData.password: A dummy password for practice. Never put a real password in a file you share.
notes.spec: The desired state: what you want Kubernetes to run.
notes.spec.containers: The containers in this Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.containers[].name: The container's name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.containers[].image: A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.containers[].command: The command to run. It prints the username, then sleeps so you can look around.
notes.spec.containers[].env: Environment variables for this container, one per list item.
notes.spec.containers[].env[].name: The variable name the app reads: DB_USER.
notes.spec.containers[].env[].valueFrom: Take the value from another object instead of writing it here.
notes.spec.containers[].env[].valueFrom.secret: Read the value from one key of a Secret.
The key inside the Secret: username.

tryIt.result: Prints secret/db-login created and pod/secret-demo created.
The values appear base64-encoded under data, not encrypted.
Removes the Secret and the Pod.
